messages:
incident-bot: Pager: SLO Alert: hosted-inference.p99_latency > 2.0s over 10m for service 'generation-streaming'. Affected pool: shared-gpu-pool-3. Severity: P2. Runbook: https://ops.redwood/alerts/1802504321

maria: I'm on it — opening live console. p95 ~ 300ms but p99 climbing to 2.3s, seeing streaming stalls and partial responses.

ken: seeing high blocked I/O on gpu-node-17, iostat shows %iowait spiking to ~40% on nvme0

tara: any tenant hotspots? run `redwoodctl tenant top --pool=shared-gpu-pool-3`

maria: running that now...

maria: output: tenant t-984 (jdoe@acme) sending ~6k concurrent streams, sustained throughput, large per-request batch sizes.

slo-monitor: auto-metric: streamed-segment-stalls increased x5; correlated with tenant t-984 traffic and node gpu-node-17 metrics.

ken: `kubectl exec -it gpu-node-17 -- iotop -boP` shows a container writing heavy overlayfs churn, PID 34211 (container: tenant-t-984-preproc). Also seeing cpu.throttling_event_count increment in cgroup for the runtime.

maria: suspicious — could be noisy neighbor doing heavy preprocessing writes + large model batches.

maria: Proposed quick mitigations: 1) throttle tenant t-984 via cgroup cpu shares & ionice. 2) migrate tenant to dedicated-spot pool. 3) disable large-batching for t-984. 4) restart worker if NVMe queues remain stuck.

ken: applying throttle: `cgset -r cpu.shares=128 /redwood/tenants/t-984` and set `ionice -c2 -n7` for the container process.

(2m later)
ken: cgset applied, ionice set. Observed immediate reduction in iowait on gpu-node-17, p99 dropped from ~2.3s -> 1.1s. p95 unchanged.

maria: kicking off migration: `redwoodctl migrate-tenant t-984 --to=dedicated-spot-2 --drain=true` — this will move active sessions and avoid further shared-pool contention.

(6m later)
maria: migration in progress, connections draining on shared-gpu-pool-3 for t-984. slo-monitor shows p99 at 0.42s and streaming stalls back to baseline. :thumbsup:

dave: any customer-visible errors / 5xxs?

maria: brief partial session resets recorded — ~12 sessions from acme (tenant t-984). Logged as INC-2026-774. Majority of customers unaffected.

ken: filed infra follow-up: investigate overlayfs churn from tenant preproc container, suspect unbounded temp file writes causing NVMe saturation and raising IO wait. Ticket INFRA-2026-312.

tara: fallback options if migration didn't reduce SLOs — enable q8 quantized model for noisy tenant or route to a lower-latency variant. Also consider per-tenant burst rate limits.

maria: enabled model-fallback for t-984 to `gpt-small-q8` for 15m as a safety net, and disabled request-batching overrides for that tenant.

ops-bot: Note: restarted worker redwood-worker-gpu-17 at 1802505200 to clear NVMe queue and stuck threads (actioned by ken).

maria: post-restart p99 stable at ~0.38s. Continuing to monitor for 30m. Muting alert channel for 20m to avoid noise. :white_check_mark:

ken: prepping handoff to @dave (next oncall) — summary: noisy tenant t-984 caused IO and cgroup throttling on gpu-node-17, mitigated by cgroup throttling + ionice, tenant migration to dedicated pool, temporary model-fallback, and worker restart. Remaining action items: infra to analyze overlayfs writes and recommend tenant-side fixes (INFRA-2026-312), consider adding per-tenant IO quotas and burst rate-limiter.
dave: ack — I'll own the watch from 1802505960. If regression, will escalate to infra and unmute paging.

maria: Handoff notes appended to INC-2026-774. Estimated customer impact window ~15m, ~12 sessions saw resets. Customer Success notified to reach out to acme.

slo-monitor: SLO alert cleared at 1802505405 (p99 back under threshold).

maria: handing off now. /me signs out. :wave:
